items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Are there any particular pieces — Stravinsky or anything like that

ctx.x: exactly what’s written. Because it’s easy to confuse a figure with something else. It’s easy to poke in a note. And those are some of the considerations. Technically — there were some technical things too.
How about classical experiences? Are there any particular pieces — Stravinsky or anything like that — you’ve ever had really challenging work in the symphonic world?
Yeah. I recorded “Forest of the Amazon” with Villa Lobos and that had some moments. And there are a number of symphonic things. Yeah. There were moments, a lot of moments.
